title: 'Gunna smash him': Shock KO tip as Kangaroos stars eye surprise role - Gal vs NAS LIVE
text: ‘Gunna smash him’: Shock KO tip as Kangaroos stars eye surprise role — Gal vs NAS LIVE ‘Gunna smash him’: Shock KO tip as Kangaroos stars eye surprise role — Gal vs NAS LIVE Australia’s Kangaroo stars are divided when it comes to picking a winner in tonight’s crossover blockbuster between Paul Gallen and Nelson Asofa-Solomona – with players having even offered to walk both fighters to the ring. Ahead of this Sunday’s World Cup semi-final against Samoa, a large group of Kangaroos have offered up their tips for tonight’s No Limit heavyweight showdown at Tik Tok Arena. Gallen v Asofa-Solomona | Friday November 6 from 7pm AEDT | Australian sporting icon and crossover boxing king Paul Gallen returns to the ring to face his biggest opponent yet, Nelson ‘Big Nasty’ Asofa-Solomona.| It’s understood Latrell Mitchell also heads a small group of Aussies who are keen to attend the fights, while as late as Friday morning there were also whispers about players potentially joining in the ring walks. Elsewhere, Fox Sports Australia can also reveal Asofa-Solomona knocked out a sparring partner during camp with a thunderous straight right – and his team are now quietly tipping him to finish Gal with the exact same punch.It comes as the NSW Origin great has himself taken one final dig at ‘Big Nasty’, accusing the almost 140kg athlete of trying to emulate the late, great Muhammad Ali. Latrell Mitchell and Tim Tszyu are both keen to witness Paul Gallen vs Nelson Asofa-Solomona. Earlier this week inside their Cup camp, Mitchell took to Instagram asking players for their heavyweight picks – with Gal getting up nine votes to four.Most notably, Reece Walsh and Cam Murray both backed the former Blues skipper to win what shapes as a $1 million bounty by finishing his monstrous rival in the fourth round. Aussie forward Tino Fa’asuamaleaui, however, put himself in the opposite corner, saying: “Big Nasty, the uso, gonna smash him”. Harry Grant and Cam Munster, unsurprisingly, are also backing the former Stormer, as is backrower Isaah Yeo.Bradman Best, however, leads a group of players backing Gal, convinced the experience of a man who has faced the likes of Justis Huni, Mark Hunt and Lucas Browne will get him home. Weight drama strikes Gallen v NAS card as legend takes aim, fight call made Meanwhile, Gal accused NAS of trying to be like American boxing icon Ali when they were up close during several face offs in fight week.“The other day it was something about beating me in three, it seems he’s really big on them at the moment. Gallen also remains unstressed about the size and reach difference in Friday’s headliner.“I’ve survived at 5’10’’ for 25 years,” he shrugged of his famed sporting career. “And growing up in western Sydney, I’ve also seen guys like Nelson my whole life. “Because while he may be big and strong, I know that when push comes to shove, and he really gets tested, he won’t be there. And that’s why I’m going to be constantly harassing him.On him like a rash. ” Elsewhere, Gallen’s fight team have stressed the 45-year-old will have no issue keeping up with the former New Zealand Test prop – and despite conceding 15 years to his rival. Paul Gallen and Nelson Asofa-Solomona face off during the weigh in ahead of Paul Gallen v Nelson Asofa-Solomona, at Tik Tok Entertainment Centre on November 05, 2026 in Sydney, Australia.In fact, Gal’s longtime trainer – Shire exercise physiologist Justin Lang – says the ageing Cronulla great still regularly competes, and betters, NRL players who enter his gym for sessions.“Right now, Gal would be less than eight per cent off what was his mark at his peak,” Lang said. “He’s just unrelenting. He also has a mindset that his competitors don’t … it’s why he wins more often than not. ” Meanwhile, the anticipated undercard fight between Ahmad Reda and Jake Wyllie will be going ahead after both fighters made weight at a rescheduled fight day weigh-in.Reda branded the miss “embarrassing” before then promising to still knock him out. No Limit boss George Rose later confirmed the fight would still go ahead, albeit with an agreement that both fighters would hit the scales again Friday morning, with Wyllie needing to be no heavier than 67.6kg. Back on the main event, meanwhile, and Gal undoubtedly has the majority of Australian players backing him.When addressing media earlier this week however, Asofa-Solomona insisted that several of the Shire tough’s former team-mates had privately urged him to knock the now Channel Nine NRL analyst out.“There’s been so many people jumping in my DMs,” NAS said. “People who’ve played with Gal, people who’ve played against him, even people who have worked with him in the past. “They’ve been telling me all these stories about him. Saying ‘yeah, bro, like please do a job on him’ …” Asked to expand on the stories, the former New Zealand Test prop continued: “I can’t say too much, it’s stuff to do with money.Bits and pieces. Pushed on the messages, and if they had actually come from former Cronulla and NSW Origin stars, and NAS grinned: “They’re the only two teams he’s played for... ”Paul Gallen vs Nelson Asofa-Solomona: Heavyweight Ahmad Reda vs Jake Wyllie: Lightweight Blair Geraghty vs Peter Lee: Super Lightweight
